tool_calling_support: coopforge box 'agentic-bielik-for-the-win-1' serves model id 'bielik-minitron-7b' = weights speakleash/Bielik-Minitron-7B-v3.0-Instruct (HF created 2026-01-22, apache-2.0, ChatML template, 7.48B BF16, pruned from Bielik-11B-v3-Base-20250730). So this IS the latest v3.0 release, not an old version; the outline's 'old version without trained tool-calling' suspicion is disproven on the version axis. Remaining suspicion: engine. Box runs image ollama/ollama:latest serving a Q4_K_M GGUF with no evidence of the official bielik advanced chat template or tool parser — native server-side tool-call parsing likely absent [uncertain: coopforge_tool_calling_native]. SpeakLeash ships official tool-calling for this exact model via bielik-tools (github.com/speakleash/bielik-tools, MIT): vLLM plugin bielik_vllm_tool_parser.py registered as parser 'bielik' (extracts <tool_call>{json}</tool_call>, streaming-capable, supports_required_and_named=False, tool_choice=required redirected to auto+guided regex) plus bielik_advanced_chat_template.jinja; vLLM >= 0.24.0 current, 0.15.0-0.23.x legacy variant file. For Ollama/GGUF the official GGUF README provides a second Modfile 'Ollama Modfile with tools' that injects tool schemas into the system turn and expects a bare JSON {name,arguments} reply (author: Kuba Soltys). The stock tokenizer chat_template is bare ChatML with no tools branch, so a vanilla Ollama container exposes none of this.

Prompt+tools budget <=3k tokens holds (770 + 6 tool schemas).

backend_serving: Coopforge backend = plain Ollama: engine image ollama/ollama:latest, Q4_K_M GGUF, no bielik advanced template/parser observed on the box page or status page [uncertain: coopforge_tool_calling_native]. vLLM reference serving for the same weights (speakleash/bielik-tools README): vllm serve speakleash/Bielik-Minitron-7B-v3.0-Instruct --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-parser-plugin ./tools/bielik_vllm_tool_parser.py --tool-call-parser bielik --chat-template ./tools/bielik_advanced_chat_template.jinja (parser flag is 'bielik', NOT 'hermes'; hermes parser is for Qwen-family tags). Ollama path: official GGUF README 'Modfile with tools' (ChatML + system-injected tool schemas + bare-JSON tool replies) — requires re-creating the coopforge model with that Modfile. llama.cpp path: stock ChatML template emits no tool structure; omp's client-side hermes dialect (packages/ai/src/dialect/hermes.ts, tools.format=hermes or PI_DIALECT=hermes) is the fallback that formats tool calls in-prompt and parses text replies. B200-class vLLM availability for this model unverified [uncertain: vllm_b200_availability].
tool_call_rate: Phase-0 curl gate (tests/bielik-gateway-test.sh, 20x POST 127.0.0.1:4000/v1/chat/completions, model coopforge/bielik-minitron-7b, single tool get_time, tool_choice auto, 60s timeout): 20/20 valid tool_calls, 0 malformed, valid_tool_calls_pct 100.0 (tests/bielik-gateway-results.json) — but with exactly 1 tool and a short prompt. omp suite (omp-bielik-tasks.sh, TASK_TIMEOUT 300): v1 broad tools 33% pass (9 tasks run of 12, run cancelled; passes: cli-python-version, cli-grep, cli-git-status) with all 4 edit-* tasks failing at 199-301s; v2 narrow tools 16% pass (full 12 tasks; only cli-grep and cli-git-status pass; every edit task 0, wall 274-301s; git/log/cli-ls also 0). Edit-tool usage 0/8 across both variants. Cross-run stability: pass set shrinks v1->v2, wall times cluster at timeout ceiling -> failures dominated by timeout/no-completion, not malformed JSON. Verdict: tool-calling works only in trivial 1-tool short-prompt regime; agentic multi-tool edit loop fails.
streaming_behavior: Coopforge caps 1 concurrent stream/member, 50k TPM. LiteLLM route sets drop_params (drops web_search_options) and max_tokens 8192; no stream-specific options; context_window_fallbacks [] (fail loud). Suite wall times hitting the 300s TASK_TIMEOUT on all edit tasks and most v2 tasks indicate throughput-bound sessions at 7 tok/s rather than stream corruption. Whether tool_call deltas survive SSE chunking through LiteLLM from the coopforge Ollama backend was not directly exercised in isolation [uncertain: coopforge_tool_calling_native] — the Phase-0 gate used non-streaming completions; the bielik vLLM parser itself implements extract_tool_calls_streaming with partial-JSON diffing, so a vLLM re-serve would stream tool calls correctly.
reasoning_core_gate: Gate exists as .omp/extensions/reasoning_core_gate.ts; alias auto-discovers it walking up from PWD and loads via -e because --no-extensions disables discovery. reasoning-core doctor states: omp_installed, omp_loaded, omp_authenticated, omp_qualified; REQUIRED_EVIDENCE = allowed_write, denied_unchanged, receipt_verified, child_guard_retained, restrictions_verified; qualification invalidates on host_sha256 change (src/_omp_doctor.py). Current status: doctor 0/4, runtime unverified — gate wired but not exercised against this backend.
pass_criteria: Bar: suite pass >=80%, <=1 retry/task, <=2 tool-errors/task; fail classes timeout vs no-tool-call vs hallucination. Actual: v1 33%, v2 16% — FAIL by large margin. Failure classification: dominant class = timeout/no-completion (wall_s pinned at 240-301s vs TASK_TIMEOUT 300); edits specifically show no-tool-call behavior (0/8 edit tool invocations; model answers in text instead of calling edit/write per SYSTEM.md rule 0). Malformed-JSON hallucination class: 0 occurrences (curl gate 0 malformed). Conclusion: current coopforge serving of bielik-minitron-7b fails the agentic bar; root cause located at serving/template layer (stock Ollama + bare ChatML, no bielik tool template/parser), not at model version — v3.0-Instruct weights have official trained tool-calling via bielik-tools.
